newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania central bank to compute leu rate daily.
newsitem.headline: Romania central bank to compute leu rate daily.

text.p: Romania's central bank (BNR) said on Tuesday it would compute a daily exchange rate for the leu as an average of prices on the local foreign exchange market, to replace the former leu reference rate.
"The new system reflecting the daily realities of the interbank foreign exchange market will take effect starting March 12," the BNR said in a statement.
Last month, the BNR gave up computing the leu's reference rate after restoring local dealer licences to 24 banks, which are now market makers along with four others.

It had postponed announcing a new method of computing the exchange rate for two weeks in a row, after freezing the reference rate at its latest value of 7,744 lei to the dollar, computed on February 19. That rate was still in force until midnight, March 11.
"The new computing method remains confidential," BNR spokesman Mugur Stet told Reuters, without elaborating. The new rate would be announced sometimes next week.

The old reference rate, computed since August 1994 when the BNR introduced a free-floating foreign exchange market, was a weighted average based on daily reports of market operators. It was a guidance rate used for statistical accounting purposes.
The BNR said the new rate, which serves only statistical purposes, would be sent daily to the finance ministry, the customs as well as to the prosecution and police.
A list of daily rates would be issued weekly to the media.
The BNR also said that companies would have to use the exchange rates set by the banks where they hold their accounts, to reflect deals in their book-keeping.
Banks' quotes on screens have been showing wide ranges over the past month, compared with the uniform previous policy, when the market had been curbed to only four dealers.
On Friday, dealers' quotes ranged from 6,200/900 to 7,400/8,400 against the dollar.
